title: RetNet retention at nano scale: parallel == recurrent to 3e-7, and the decay schedule is worth 12.7x the seed noise
hypothesis: Hand-rolled multi-scale retention reproduces the RetNet parallel/recurrent duality to floating-point precision (max abs logit deviation <= ~1e-5); on a tiny char LM at matched params/steps retention trails softmax attention in val bits/char; and the decay schedule (multi-scale geometric vs uniform vs no-decay vs learned) makes a difference smaller than seed-to-seed noise.
question: Is the RetNet duality numerically exact at nano scale, does retention actually trail softmax attention on a char LM at matched budget, and does the decay schedule gamma_h matter at all?
method: Hand-rolled multi-scale retention in pure PyTorch (no yet-another-retnet dependency), implemented TWICE: parallel form Y=(Q K^T . D)V with D[n,m]=gamma_h^(n-m) on the causal triangle, and recurrent form S_t = gamma_h S_{t-1} + k_t^T v_t, y_t = q_t S_t, sharing an identical post-path (headwise GroupNorm -> swish gate -> output projection) so any gap is pure float error. Model: 2 pre-norm blocks, d_model 64, 4 heads (d_head 16), d_ff 192, ctx 128, char vocab 65, learned absolute position embeddings, 108,032 params. Reference arm: standard causal softmax MHA, iso-parameter by binary-searching its d_ff to 225 -> 108,098 params (0.061% spread). Four retention arms differ ONLY in gamma: (i) paper multi-scale 1-2^-(5+h) = .96875/.984375/.992188/.996094, (ii) uniform .97, (iii) no decay 1.0 (= pure causal linear attention), (iv) learned sigmoid(theta_h) initialised at the multi-scale values. All 5 arms: tiny-shakespeare char level 90/10 split, 800 steps, batch 16 x ctx 128 (1.64M tokens), AdamW lr 2e-3 (60-step warmup, cosine to 10%), wd 0.1, clip 1.0, IDENTICAL seeded batch stream, 2 seeds. Metric: val bits/char on a fixed 40-batch held-out set. Equivalence measured at T in {16,32,64,128} on both freshly-initialised and trained weights.
architecture: hand-rolled RetNet multi-scale retention (parallel + recurrent forms) vs softmax attention, 2-layer pre-norm char LM, d_model 64, 4 heads, d_ff 192/225, ctx 128, 0.108M params

dataset.name: tiny-shakespeare (char-level)
dataset.license: public domain text; char-rnn repo MIT

compute: CPU 1 thread, 567s (9.5 min) for 10 training runs + equivalence checks

metrics.headline: parallel vs recurrent max abs logit deviation 3.0e-07 at init / 4.8e-06 trained, FLAT in sequence length (rel dev ~1 float32 epsilon); decay-schedule spread 0.2469 bpc = 12.7x the 0.0195 seed spread, ranking learned 3.150 < uniform-.97 3.271 < attention 3.274 < paper multi-scale 3.298 < no-decay 3.397

result_summary: Two of three hypotheses held; the third was refuted hard. (1) DUALITY CONFIRMED and it is float32-exact: same weights, same batch, parallel vs recurrent max abs logit deviation is 2.4-3.0e-07 at init and 2.4-4.8e-06 after training, with max RELATIVE deviation 1.4-3.4e-07 (~one float32 epsilon) and FLAT in sequence length across T=16/32/64/128 - the recurrence does not drift - identical for all four decay schedules including gamma=1. That beats the ~1e-5 target by 2-40x. Honest aside: on CPU the Python-loop recurrent form is 4.4x SLOWER than the parallel one at B=4,T=128 (28.9 vs 6.5 ms); the recurrent form's win is asymptotic/memory, not wall clock at this size. (2) RETENTION vs ATTENTION is a wash at matched budget: the paper's multi-scale retention trails iso-parameter softmax attention by only +0.0239 bpc (1.2 seed-spreads), and uniform-gamma retention ties it (-0.0032). (3) THE DECAY SCHEDULE IS THE BIG LEVER - the pre-registered null is dead. Spread across the four schedules is 0.2469 bpc = 12.7x the max seed spread (0.0195), every adjacent pair fully seed-separated: learned 3.1496 < uniform .97 3.2706 < attention 3.2738 < paper multi-scale 3.2977 < no-decay (pure causal linear attention) 3.3965. Three sub-findings: (a) removing decay entirely is the worst arm by 0.10 bpc, so the decay is load-bearing not cosmetic; (b) ONE tuned scalar gamma shared by all heads BEATS the paper's geometric multi-scale ladder by 0.027 bpc in both seeds, so multi-scale-ness is not what pays; (c) what pays is the TIMESCALE - a naked sigmoid-parameterised learned gamma (8 extra params total) pulls every head DOWN from its multi-scale init in both layers and both seeds, half-lives 22/44/88/177 chars -> 7.5/16/29/57 chars (seed agreement +-1 char), and wins by 0.124 bpc over attention (6.4 seed-spreads); its lead over uniform GROWS monotonically through training (behind at step 200, -0.121 by step 800), so it is not an early-training artifact. Framed against this lab's zoology rows, both results are one fact from two sides: on MQAR, decay-gated linear attention sits on the query-ignoring guessing floor (2026-07-25_zoology-mqar-recall, 2026-07-26_mqar-state-capacity); here it matches attention on language - and optimisation got there by choosing to FORGET FASTER (7-57 char half-lives inside a 128-char window). The decay that buys bits/char is precisely the decay that destroys recall. Caveats: undertrained (800 steps / 1.64M tokens, all curves still descending, absolute bpc 3.15-3.40), 0.108M params, ctx 128 - short enough that two of the paper's four heads barely decay at all inside the window, which limits how far 'multi-scale loses' generalises - iso-hyperparameter rather than per-arm-tuned LR, no xPos (learned absolute position embeddings shared with the attention arm instead), 2 seeds.

novelty_check.conclusion: The mechanism is fully published, the specific comparison is not. RetNet (2307.08621) defines the parallel/recurrent/chunkwise forms and the gamma_h = 1 - 2^-(5+h) schedule, asserts the duality without publishing a numerical deviation, and its ablation table varies the gate / GroupNorm / architecture - NOT the decay schedule. fkodom/yet-another-retnet ships unit tests asserting parallel/recurrent/chunkwise agreement, so equivalence testing per se is not new; what we add is a measured deviation-vs-sequence-length curve at both freshly-initialised and trained weights. 'Disentangle to Decay' (COLING 2025, 2025.coling-main.660) makes decay factors trainable for linear attention at 137M on OpenWebText and reports gains over fixed and directly-trained decay, but states explicitly that it does NOT compare against RetNet. To our search no published work puts the four schedules - paper multi-scale vs one uniform scalar vs no decay vs learned - head to head under a single matched-everything control (iso-param 0.061%, iso-step, identical batch stream, 2 seeds) with softmax attention as an iso-parameter reference, and none does so at <=1M params on char-level data; the finding that the paper's own schedule loses to a single tuned scalar is, to our search, unreported. arXiv/OpenAlex APIs 403 from this environment (scripts/novelty_check.py returned 'unchecked'); verdict rests on web search plus a direct read of the COLING paper.
